mcqs.learning_point: Understand watt as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines the unit "watt"?

options.C: One kilogram meter per second squared

mcqs.explanation: A watt is the SI unit of power and is defined as the transfer of one joule of energy per second. Option A states this definition. Option B describes a joule (energy), option C is a unit of force (newton), and option D is a unit of pressure, none of which define power.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to work and time
mcqs.question: A person does 500 joules of work in 25 seconds. What is the power developed?
mcqs.explanation: Power is work divided by time: P = W / t = 500 J / 25 s = 20 W. Hence option B is correct. The other values result from incorrect division.

mcqs.question: Two electrical appliances are used for the same 2‑hour period: a 60 W bulb and a 1000 W heater. Which device consumes more electrical energy?

options.A: The 60 W bulb consumes more energy
options.B: The 1000 W heater consumes more energy
options.C: Both consume the same amount of energy
options.D: Cannot determine without knowing the voltage

mcqs.answer: The 1000 W heater consumes more energy
mcqs.explanation: Energy consumed = power × time. For the same time, the appliance with the higher power rating uses more energy. The heater (1000 W) therefore consumes far more energy than the 60 W bulb. Voltage is irrelevant for this comparison.

mcqs.question: Power is best described as:

options.A: Rate at which work is done

mcqs.answer: Rate at which work is done
mcqs.explanation: Power quantifies how quickly work is performed or energy is transferred, i.e., the rate of doing work. Option A captures this definition. Options B, C, and D describe work, energy, and force respectively, not power.

mcqs.question: A student calculates the power of a machine that does 200 J of work in 4 s as 800 W. Which statement is correct?

options.D: Power cannot be calculated from the given data

mcqs.explanation: Power = work / time = 200 J / 4 s = 50 W. The student's answer of 800 W is a miscalculation (perhaps multiplying instead of dividing). Therefore option B is correct; the other options repeat the error or claim impossibility.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand watt as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Why is the watt considered the SI unit for power?

options.A: Because it is defined as one joule per second, a derived SI unit
options.B: Because it measures force, which is an SI base unit
options.C: Because it measures pressure, which is an SI derived unit
options.D: Because it is equivalent to a newton, an SI unit of force

mcqs.answer: Because it is defined as one joule per second, a derived SI unit
mcqs.explanation: The watt is a derived SI unit equal to one joule of energy transferred each second, directly representing power. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated quantities (force, pressure, and newton).

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to work and time
mcqs.question: Person A does 100 J of work in 5 s, while Person B does 200 J of work in 20 s. Who has the greater power?

options.A: Person A has the greater power
options.B: Person B has the greater power
options.D: Power cannot be compared without knowing the masses involved

mcqs.answer: Person A has the greater power
mcqs.explanation: Power A = 100 J / 5 s = 20 W. Power B = 200 J / 20 s = 10 W. Hence Person A’s power is double that of Person B. Option A is correct; the other options are false or irrelevant.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the power rating of electrical appliances is true?

options.A: A higher power rating means the appliance uses more energy per unit time
options.B: Two appliances with the same power rating will always consume the same total energy
options.C: Power rating is independent of the voltage supplied
options.D: Power rating indicates the maximum energy that can be stored in the appliance

mcqs.answer: A higher power rating means the appliance uses more energy per unit time
mcqs.explanation: Power rating specifies the maximum rate of energy consumption; a larger rating implies greater energy use per second. Option B is false because total energy also depends on usage time. Option C is incorrect because power = voltage × current, so voltage matters. Option D confuses power with energy storage.
